# Contributing

Thank you for wanting to contribute. This document defines the conventions that apply to all repositories in the organization.

---

## Workflow

1. Create a branch from `develop`.
2. Make your changes with commits that follow the convention described below.
3. Open a Pull Request using the template available in the repo.
4. The PR must pass all CI checks before it can merge.
5. At least one approved review is required (CODEOWNERS is assigned automatically).

---

## Branches

The branch name must follow this format:

```
<type>/<description-in-kebab-case>
```

Valid types:
| Type | When to use it |
|---|---|
| `feature` | New functionality |
| `fix` | Bug fix |
| `hotfix` | Urgent fix direct to production |
| `refactor` | Code change without altering behavior |
| `chore` | Maintenance, cleaning |
| `docs` | Documentation |
| `test` | Tests |
| `ci` | Pipelines and workflows |
| `infra` | Infrastructure as code (Terraform, Pulumi) |
| `ops` | Runtime: Docker, Kubernetes, Helm |
| `perf` | Performance improvements |
| `release` | Release preparation |

Valid examples:

```
feature/jwt-refresh-token fix/nil-pointer-scheduler infra/add-rds-module release/v1.2.0
```

---

## Commits — Conventional Commits

All commits must follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org):

```
<type>(<scope>): <short description>
[optional body]
[optional footer — BREAKING CHANGE or reference to issue]
```

Valid types are the same as for branches: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`, `ci`, `build`, `revert`, `infra`, `ops`.

Examples:

```
feat(auth): add JWT refresh token
fix: handle empty rows in CSV parser
chore(deps): upgrade Go to 1.23
infra(terraform): add RDS module for staging
```

> Commits are the basis of the **automatic changelog** generated by Semantic Release. A poorly formed commit can break versioning.

---

## Semantic Release and versioning

This project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org) automatically managed by Semantic Release based on commits:

| Commit type                                    | Increasing version        |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- |
| `fix`                                          | Patch — `1.0.x`           |
| `feat`                                         | Minor — `1.x.0`           |
| Any type with `BREAKING CHANGE` in the footer  | Major — `x.0.0`           |
| `chore`, `docs`, `style`, `ci`, `infra`, `ops` | Does not generate release |

To indicate a breaking change:

```
feat(api): remove deprecated /v1/users endpoint

BREAKING CHANGE: The /v1/users endpoint was removed. Migrate to /v2/users.
```

---

## Pull Requests

- The title of the PR must follow Conventional Commits
- it is the commit that remains in `main` after the merge.
- Use the template available in each repo; Cover the checklist before asking for a review.
- A PR must do **one thing**. If you resolve multiple concerns, open separate PRs.
- `release/*` PRs are automatically generated by Semantic Release — do not edit them manually.

---

## CI

All repositories have required checks in the PRs. A PR cannot merge if any check fails. Specific checks vary by repo and stack, but generally cover lint, tests, build, and convention validation.

---

## Report a security issue

Do not open a public issue for vulnerabilities. Check the `SECURITY.md` of the corresponding repository.
